"Create a fully 3D mobile only magical sports game set in the Harry Potter wizarding universe, focused on high-speed broom racing and the international Quidditch World Cup.

1. BROOM RACING
Create an exciting broom racing mode where players compete against other witches and wizards on magical racing circuits. Include:

- Multiple racing tracks across different wizarding locations.
- Floating checkpoints, hoops, tunnels, obstacles and dangerous shortcuts.
- Different broom models, each with unique speed, acceleration, handling and boost abilities.
- Broom upgrades and customisation.
- Practice, qualifying, time trials and championship races.
- AI opponents with different skill levels.
- Dynamic weather, wind, storms and changing track conditions.

2. QUIDDITCH WORLD CUP
Build a complete Quidditch competition where players can represent different wizarding nations.

Include all traditional positions:

- Chaser: Score goals using the Quaffle.
- Beater: Protect teammates and hit Bludgers.
- Keeper: Defend the three goal hoops.
- Seeker: Chase and catch the Golden Snitch.

Create proper team-based Quidditch matches with AI teammates, opposing teams, match tactics, substitutions and tournament progression.

3. INTERNATIONAL MAPS
Build multiple large, beautifully detailed 3D environments inspired by the wizarding world:

- Hogwarts grounds and surrounding countryside.
- The Quidditch World Cup stadium.
- Scottish Highlands.
- London wizarding district.
- Enchanted forests.
- Snow-covered mountain circuits.
- International magical stadiums inspired by different countries.

Each location should have unique racing circuits, Quidditch stadiums, scenery, obstacles and environmental effects.

4. CAREER AND PROGRESSION
Start as an aspiring young broom athlete and work your way towards becoming a world champion.

Include:

- Player creation and character customisation.
- Unlockable brooms and equipment.
- Training challenges and skill progression.
- National team selection.
- International championships.
- Trophies, rankings, rewards and achievements.
- A career history showing race and Quidditch statistics.

5. PRESENTATION
Use beautiful 3D graphics, cinematic camera angles, smooth broom flight animations, realistic flying physics and exciting stadium crowds.

Include magical sound effects, commentator reactions, crowd chants, victory celebrations and dramatic tournament introductions.

IMPORTANT: Make this feel like a complete magical sports game rather than a simple flying simulator. Both broom racing and Quidditch must be fully playable, with their own progression systems, competitions, maps and rewards. Build upon the existing game world if one already exists rather than replacing it.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

const makeLoop = (o) => {
 const pts=[];
 for(i=0;i<o.count;i++){

 }
 return pts;
}

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable mobile-only 3D magical sports game featuring broom racing and a Quidditch World Cup, extending the existing game world where present.

## Requirements
- Include racing tracks, broom models/upgrades/customisation, race modes, AI opponents, and dynamic weather.
- Include all four Quidditch positions, team play, AI teammates/opponents, tactics, and tournament progression.
- Provide wizarding-inspired environments, career progression, customisation, rewards, and polished audiovisual presentation.
- Make reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions; briefly note them when finishing.
- Save small JPEG screenshots for checks (viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Implemented as a Vite app using Three.js, procedural visuals/audio, and browser-local save progression.
- Uses original wizarding-inspired names and settings.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built game data, persistence/progression, audio, procedural 3D worlds, racing, Quidditch, UI, and app orchestration.
- Added mobile-first UI styling, Vite setup, and app entry markup.
- Fixed race “GO!” overlay persistence and added a data-URI favicon.
- Improved Quidditch hoop placement with depth separation, support arms, and lighting/materials for better stadium visibility; adjusted opponent scoreboard padding.
- Tested onboarding, home, race hub/briefing/start, and Quidditch tournament/match flow in a mobile-sized browser.
- Saved and inspected gameplay JPEG screenshots under `screenshots/`.
- `npm run build` passed before the latest visual changes.

### Active
- Re-run the production build and check browser console/runtime after the newest stadium and UI edits.
- Capture and inspect the latest screenshot, then finish any remaining visual or interaction fixes.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run `npm run build`.
2. Reload the app, check race and Quidditch controls/console, and verify recent hoop, lighting, and scoreboard changes.
3. Save a small JPEG screenshot and inspect only the latest screenshot.
4. Summarize the delivered features and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: App orchestration and boot code.
- `src/ui.js`: Menus, HUD, and modal UI.
- `src/race.js`: Broom-racing game logic.
- `src/quidditch.js`: Quidditch match logic.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Finish and visually verify the mobile-first broom racing and Quidditch game, focusing on active-match presentation, flight, shooting, and mobile HUD usability.

## Requirements
- Prioritize mobile visuals and approachable flight and shooting controls.
- Check HUD/control overlap, readability, and gameplay framing.

## Decisions
- Retain adaptive renderer resolution and mobile-tuned settings.
- Use eased analog controls and forgiving Chaser hoop aim assistance.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Finish and visually verify the mobile-first broom racing and Quidditch game, focusing on active-match presentation, flight, shooting, and mobile HUD usability.

## Requirements
- Prioritize mobile visuals and approachable flight and shooting controls.
- Check HUD/control overlap, readability, and gameplay framing.

## Decisions
- Retain adaptive renderer resolution and mobile-tuned settings.
- Use eased analog controls and forgiving Chaser hoop aim assistance.
- Keep the Quidditch stadium perimeter wall low to preserve the low-flight camera’s view.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added adaptive pixel-ratio scaling, a larger repositionable joystick, eased controls, Chaser aim assistance, target highlighting, and HUD guidance.
- Reduced Quidditch stadium perimeter wall height in `src/world.js`.
- Reached an active Quidditch match at 390×844 mobile size and captured `/tmp/opencode/mobile-gameplay-active-check.png`.
- Confirmed nation colors in `src/data.js` and the stadium color palette are valid hex values.

### Active
- Assess active-match framing, readability, and HUD/control overlap using the screenshot.
- Trace repeated Three.js warnings: `THREE.Color: Unknown color #`, `THREE.Color: Unknown color 3/4/6`; searched color constructors and stadium palette without finding the source.

### Blocked
- Node-based warning tracing fails with `ReferenceError: document is not defined` because world creation uses browser canvas APIs; investigate in the browser.

## Next Move
1. Assess `/tmp/opencode/mobile-gameplay-active-check.png` for gameplay framing and HUD/control overlap.
2. Trace the invalid Three.js color warnings in the browser.
3. Fix any issues found, rebuild, and recapture/verify the active match.

## Relevant Files
- `src/world.js`: Quidditch stadium/world setup and color construction.
- `src/quidditch.js`: Match camera, flight, shooting, aim assistance, and gameplay state.
- `src/ui.js`: Quidditch HUD and gameplay controls.
- `src/styles.css`: Mobile HUD and control styling.
- `src/data.js`: Nation color definitions.
- `src/main.js`: Renderer setup and game flow.
- `/tmp/opencode/mobile-gameplay-active-check.png`: Active-match mobile screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `dist/` contains modified generated assets, deleted old bundles, and new bundles.
- Dev server is at `http://127.0.0.1:3002/`; the active match was running in the browser.
- Browser snapshot reported 0 errors and 30 warnings, including GPU `ReadPixels` stalls and repeated invalid Three.js color warnings.
- Current Chaser objective reads “Steer toward the glowing hoop and SHOOT · MIDDLE HOOP LINED UP.”

## Objective
- Finish and visually verify the mobile-first broom racing and Quidditch game, focusing on active-match presentation, flight, shooting, and mobile HUD usability.

## Requirements
- Prioritize mobile visuals and approachable flight and shooting controls.
- Check HUD/control overlap, readability, and gameplay framing.

## Decisions
- Retain adaptive renderer resolution and mobile-tuned settings.
- Use eased analog controls and forgiving Chaser hoop aim assistance.
- Keep the Quidditch stadium perimeter wall low to preserve the low-flight camera’s view.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added adaptive pixel-ratio scaling, a larger repositionable joystick, eased controls, Chaser aim assistance, target highlighting, and HUD guidance.
- Reached an active Quidditch match at 390×844 mobile size and captured `/tmp/opencode/mobile-gameplay-active-check.png`.
- Confirmed nation colors and the stadium color palette use valid hex values.

### Active
- Assess active-match framing, readability, and HUD/control overlap using the screenshot.
- Trace repeated Three.js warnings: `THREE.Color: Unknown color #`, `THREE.Color: Unknown color 3/4/6`; searched color constructors and stadium palette without finding the source.

### Blocked
- Node-based warning tracing fails with `ReferenceError: document is not defined` because world creation uses browser canvas APIs; continue investigation in the browser.

## Next Move
1. Assess `/tmp/opencode/mobile-gameplay-active-check.png` for gameplay framing and HUD/control overlap.
2. Trace the invalid Three.js color warnings in the browser.
3. Fix any issues found, rebuild, and recapture/verify the active match.

## Relevant Files
- `src/world.js`: Quidditch stadium/world setup and color construction.
- `src/quidditch.js`: Match camera, flight, shooting, aim assistance, and gameplay state.
- `src/ui.js`: Quidditch HUD and gameplay controls.
- `src/styles.css`: Mobile HUD and control styling.
- `src/data.js`: Nation color definitions.
- `src/main.js`: Renderer setup and game flow.
- `/tmp/opencode/mobile-gameplay-active-check.png`: Active-match mobile screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `dist/` contains modified generated assets, deleted old bundles, and new bundles.
- Dev server is at `http://127.0.0.1:3002/`; Chromium is running headless at 390×844 with remote debugging on port 9222.
- Browser snapshot reported 0 errors and 30 warnings, including GPU `ReadPixels` stalls and repeated invalid Three.js color warnings.
- Current Chaser objective reads “Steer toward the glowing hoop and SHOOT · MIDDLE HOOP LINED UP.”

## Objective
- Finish and visually verify the mobile-first broom racing and Quidditch game, focusing on active-match presentation, flight, shooting, and mobile HUD usability.

## Requirements
- Prioritize mobile visuals and approachable flight and shooting controls.
- Check HUD/control overlap, readability, and gameplay framing.

## Decisions
- Retain adaptive renderer resolution and mobile-tuned settings.
- Use eased analog controls and forgiving Chaser hoop aim assistance.
- Keep the Quidditch stadium perimeter wall low to preserve the low-flight camera’s view.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added adaptive pixel-ratio scaling, a larger repositionable joystick, eased controls, Chaser aim assistance, target highlighting, and HUD guidance.
- Reached an active Quidditch match at 390×844 and captured `/tmp/opencode/mobile-gameplay-active-check.png`.
- Confirmed nation colors and stadium palette use valid hex values.

### Active
- Assess active-match framing, readability, and HUD/control overlap from the screenshot.
- Trace repeated Three.js warnings: `THREE.Color: Unknown color #`, `THREE.Color: Unknown color 3/4/6`.
- Re-enter an active match and capture console warnings with stack traces.

### Blocked
- Browser DevTools re-check did not reach gameplay: the page had no HUD elements, and a later CDP WebSocket evaluation timed out while Chromium’s GPU process was using high CPU. The DevTools HTTP endpoint at port 9222 responds.

## Next Move
1. Inspect `/tmp/opencode/mobile-gameplay-active-check.png` for gameplay framing and HUD/control overlap.
2. Restart or recover the browser session, enter an active match, and capture warning stacks and HUD element bounds.
3. Fix any issues found, rebuild, and recapture/verify the active match.

## Relevant Files
- `src/world.js`: Stadium/world setup and color construction.
- `src/quidditch.js`: Match camera, flight, shooting, aim assistance, and gameplay state.
- `src/ui.js`: Quidditch HUD and gameplay controls.
- `src/styles.css`: Mobile HUD and control styling.
- `src/data.js`: Nation color definitions.
- `src/main.js`: Renderer setup, input, and game flow.
- `/tmp/opencode/mobile-gameplay-active-check.png`: Active-match mobile screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `dist/` has modified generated assets, deleted old bundles, and new bundles.
- Dev server is at `http://127.0.0.1:3002/`; headless Chromium uses remote debugging on port 9222.
- A prior browser snapshot showed 0 errors and 30 warnings, including GPU `ReadPixels` stalls and repeated invalid Three.js color warnings. The latest reload showed only a software WebGL fallback warning and no HUD.
- Node-based warning tracing fails with `ReferenceError: document is not defined` because world creation uses browser canvas APIs.
- Recent source inspection found a stadium crowd palette passed to `tmpColor.set(...)` in `src/world.js`; no invalid palette entries were identified.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Finish and visually verify the mobile-first broom racing and Quidditch game, focusing on active-match presentation, flight, shooting, and mobile HUD usability.

## Requirements
- Prioritize mobile visuals and approachable flight and shooting controls.
- Check HUD/control overlap, readability, and gameplay framing.

## Decisions
- Retain adaptive renderer resolution and mobile-tuned settings.
- Use eased analog controls and forgiving Chaser hoop aim assistance.
- Keep the Quidditch stadium perimeter wall low to preserve the low-flight camera’s view.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added adaptive pixel-ratio scaling, a larger repositionable joystick, eased controls, Chaser aim assistance, target highlighting, and HUD guidance.
- Reached an active Quidditch match at 390×844 and captured `/tmp/opencode/mobile-gameplay-active-check.png`.
- Confirmed nation colors and stadium palette use valid hex values.

### Active
- Assess active-match framing, readability, and HUD/control overlap from the captured screenshot.
- Trace repeated Three.js warnings: `THREE.Color: Unknown color #`, `THREE.Color: Unknown color 3/4/6`.
- Re-enter an active match and capture warning stacks and HUD element bounds.

### Blocked
- Browser DevTools re-check did not reach gameplay: the page had no HUD elements, and a later CDP WebSocket evaluation timed out while Chromium’s GPU process was using high CPU. The DevTools HTTP endpoint at port 9222 responds.
- Node-based warning tracing fails with `ReferenceError: document is not defined` because world creation uses browser canvas APIs.

## Next Move
1. Inspect `/tmp/opencode/mobile-gameplay-active-check.png` for gameplay framing and HUD/control overlap.
2. Recover or restart the browser, enter an active match, and capture warning stacks and HUD element bounds.
3. Trace and fix any invalid color inputs; the inspected nation and stadium crowd palettes contain valid hex values.
4. Rebuild and recapture/verify the active match.

## Relevant Files
- `src/world.js`: Stadium/world setup and color construction.
- `src/quidditch.js`: Match camera, flight, shooting, aim assistance, and gameplay state.
- `src/ui.js`: Quidditch HUD and gameplay controls.
- `src/styles.css`: Mobile HUD and control styling.
- `src/data.js`: Nation color definitions.
- `src/main.js`: Renderer setup, input, and game flow.
- `/tmp/opencode/mobile-gameplay-active-check.png`: Active-match mobile screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `dist/` has modified generated assets, deleted old bundles, and new bundles.
- Dev server is at `http://127.0.0.1:3002/`; headless Chromium uses remote debugging on port 9222.
- A prior browser snapshot showed 0 errors and 30 warnings, including GPU `ReadPixels` stalls and repeated invalid Three.js color warnings. Latest reload showed only a software WebGL fallback warning and no HUD.
- Recent inspection of `src/world.js` found valid hex values in the stadium crowd palette and Quidditch tent colors; the warning source remains unresolved.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Finish and visually verify the mobile-first broom racing and Quidditch game, focusing on active-match presentation, flight, shooting, and mobile HUD usability.

## Requirements
- Prioritize mobile visuals and approachable flight and shooting controls.
- Check HUD/control overlap, readability, and gameplay framing.

## Decisions
- Retain adaptive renderer resolution and mobile-tuned settings.
- Use eased analog controls and forgiving Chaser hoop aim assistance.
- Keep the Quidditch stadium perimeter wall low to preserve the low-flight camera’s view.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added adaptive pixel-ratio scaling, a larger repositionable joystick, eased controls, Chaser aim assistance, target highlighting, and HUD guidance.
- Captured an active Quidditch match at 390×844: `/tmp/opencode/mobile-gameplay-active-check.png`.
- Confirmed nation colors and the inspected stadium/crowd palettes contain valid hex values.

### Active
- Assess active-match framing, readability, and HUD/control overlap in the captured screenshot.
- Trace repeated Three.js warnings: `THREE.Color: Unknown color #`, `THREE.Color: Unknown color 3/4/6`.
- Re-enter an active match, capture warning stacks and HUD element bounds, then rebuild and verify.

### Blocked
- Browser DevTools re-check did not reach gameplay; a later CDP WebSocket evaluation timed out while Chromium’s GPU process was using high CPU.
- Node-based warning tracing fails with `ReferenceError: document is not defined` because world creation uses browser canvas APIs.

## Next Move
1. Inspect `/tmp/opencode/mobile-gameplay-active-check.png` for gameplay framing and HUD/control overlap.
2. Recover or restart the browser, enter an active match, and capture warning stacks and HUD element bounds.
3. Trace and fix invalid color inputs; the inspected nation and stadium palette definitions are valid, so the warning source remains unresolved.
4. Rebuild and recapture/verify the active match.

## Relevant Files
- `src/world.js`: Stadium/world setup and color construction; likely place to trace invalid color values.
- `src/quidditch.js`: Match camera, flight, shooting, aim assistance, and gameplay state.
- `src/ui.js`: Quidditch HUD and gameplay controls.
- `src/styles.css`: Mobile HUD and control styling.
- `src/data.js`: Nation color definitions.
- `src/main.js`: Renderer setup, input, and game flow.
- `/tmp/opencode/mobile-gameplay-active-check.png`: Active-match mobile screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `dist/` has modified generated assets, deleted old bundles, and new bundles.
- Dev server is at `http://127.0.0.1:3002/`; headless Chromium uses remote debugging on port 9222.
- A prior browser snapshot showed 0 errors and 30 warnings, including GPU `ReadPixels` stalls and repeated invalid Three.js color warnings. Latest reload showed only a software WebGL fallback warning and no HUD.
- Latest inspection found valid nation colors in `src/data.js` and valid-looking colors at the Quidditch tent and crowd setup in `src/world.js`; warnings remain unresolved.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Finish and visually verify the mobile-first broom racing and Quidditch game, focusing on active-match presentation, flight, shooting, and mobile HUD usability.

## Requirements
- Prioritize mobile visuals and approachable flight and shooting controls.
- Check HUD/control overlap, readability, and gameplay framing.

## Decisions
- Retain adaptive renderer resolution and mobile-tuned settings.
- Use eased analog controls and forgiving Chaser hoop aim assistance.
- Keep the Quidditch stadium perimeter wall low to preserve the low-flight camera’s view.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added adaptive pixel-ratio scaling, a larger repositionable joystick, eased controls, Chaser aim assistance, target highlighting, and HUD guidance.
- Captured an active Quidditch match at 390×844: `/tmp/opencode/mobile-gameplay-active-check.png`.
- Confirmed nation colors and the inspected stadium/crowd palettes contain valid hex values.

### Active
- Assess active-match framing, readability, and HUD/control overlap in the captured screenshot.
- Re-enter an active match, capture warning stacks and HUD element bounds, and trace repeated Three.js invalid-color warnings.

### Blocked
- Browser DevTools re-check did not reach gameplay; a later CDP WebSocket evaluation timed out while Chromium’s GPU process was using high CPU.
- Node-based warning tracing fails with `ReferenceError: document is not defined` because world creation uses browser canvas APIs.

## Next Move
1. Inspect `/tmp/opencode/mobile-gameplay-active-check.png` for gameplay framing and HUD/control overlap.
2. Recover or restart the browser, enter an active match, and capture warning stacks and HUD element bounds.
3. Trace and fix `THREE.Color: Unknown color #`, `THREE.Color: Unknown color 3/4/6`; inspected nation and stadium palette definitions are valid.
4. Rebuild and recapture/verify the active match.

## Relevant Files
- `src/world.js`: Stadium/world setup and color construction; likely place to trace invalid color inputs.
- `src/quidditch.js`: Match camera, flight, shooting, aim assistance, and gameplay state.
- `src/ui.js`: Quidditch HUD and gameplay controls.
- `src/styles.css`: Mobile HUD and control styling.
- `src/data.js`: Nation color definitions.
- `src/main.js`: Renderer setup, input, and game flow.
- `/tmp/opencode/mobile-gameplay-active-check.png`: Active-match mobile screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `dist/` has modified generated assets, deleted old bundles, and new bundles.
- Dev server is at `http://127.0.0.1:3002/`; headless Chromium uses remote debugging on port 9222.
- A prior browser snapshot showed 0 errors and 30 warnings, including GPU `ReadPixels` stalls and repeated invalid Three.js color warnings. Latest reload showed only a software WebGL fallback warning and no HUD.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Finish and visually verify the mobile-first broom racing and Quidditch game, focusing on active-match presentation, flight, shooting, and mobile HUD usability.

## Requirements
- Prioritize mobile visuals and approachable flight and shooting controls.
- Check HUD/control overlap, readability, and gameplay framing.

## Decisions
- Retain adaptive renderer resolution and mobile-tuned settings.
- Use eased analog controls and forgiving Chaser hoop aim assistance.
- Keep the Quidditch stadium perimeter wall low to preserve the low-flight camera’s view.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added adaptive pixel-ratio scaling, a larger repositionable joystick, eased controls, Chaser aim assistance, target highlighting, and HUD guidance.
- Captured an active Quidditch match at 390×844: `/tmp/opencode/mobile-gameplay-active-check.png`.
- Confirmed nation colors and the inspected stadium/crowd palettes contain valid hex values.

### Active
- Assess active-match framing, readability, and HUD/control overlap in the captured screenshot.
- Recover or restart the browser, enter an active match, and capture warning stacks and HUD element bounds.
- Trace repeated Three.js invalid-color warnings to the color inputs in `src/world.js` and related call sites.

### Blocked
- Browser DevTools re-check did not reach gameplay; a later CDP WebSocket evaluation timed out while Chromium’s GPU process was using high CPU.
- Node-based warning tracing fails with `ReferenceError: document is not defined` because world creation uses browser canvas APIs.

## Next Move
1. Inspect `/tmp/opencode/mobile-gameplay-active-check.png` for gameplay framing and HUD/control overlap.
2. Recover or restart Chromium and capture an active match with warning stacks and HUD element bounds.
3. Identify and fix the source of `THREE.Color: Unknown color #`, `THREE.Color: Unknown color 3/4/6`; nation and inspected stadium palette definitions are valid.
4. Rebuild and recapture/verify the active match.

## Relevant Files
- `src/world.js`: Stadium/world setup and color construction; likely place to trace invalid color inputs.
- `src/quidditch.js`: Match camera, flight, shooting, aim assistance, and gameplay state.
- `src/ui.js`: Quidditch HUD and gameplay controls.
- `src/styles.css`: Mobile HUD and control styling.
- `src/data.js`: Nation color definitions.
- `src/main.js`: Renderer setup, input, and game flow.
- `/tmp/opencode/mobile-gameplay-active-check.png`: Active-match mobile screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `dist/` has modified generated assets, deleted old bundles, and new bundles.
- Dev server is at `http://127.0.0.1:3002/`; headless Chromium uses remote debugging on port 9222.
- A prior browser snapshot showed 0 errors and 30 warnings, including GPU `ReadPixels` stalls and repeated invalid Three.js color warnings. Latest reload showed only a software WebGL fallback warning and no HUD.

## Objective
- Finish and visually verify the mobile-first broom racing and Quidditch game, focusing on active-match presentation, flight, shooting, and mobile HUD usability.

## Requirements
- Prioritize mobile visuals and approachable flight and shooting controls.
- Check HUD/control overlap, readability, and gameplay framing.

## Decisions
- Retain adaptive renderer resolution and mobile-tuned settings.
- Use eased analog controls and forgiving Chaser hoop aim assistance.
- Keep the Quidditch stadium perimeter wall low to preserve the low-flight camera’s view.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added adaptive pixel-ratio scaling, a larger repositionable joystick, eased controls, Chaser aim assistance, target highlighting, and HUD guidance.
- Captured an active Quidditch match at 390×844: `/tmp/opencode/mobile-gameplay-active-check.png`.
- Confirmed nation colors and the inspected stadium/crowd palettes contain valid hex values.

### Active
- Assess active-match framing, readability, and HUD/control overlap in the captured screenshot.
- Recover or restart the browser, enter an active match, and capture warning stacks and HUD element bounds.
- Trace repeated Three.js invalid-color warnings to the color inputs in `src/world.js` and related call sites.

### Blocked
- Browser DevTools re-check did not reach gameplay; a later CDP WebSocket evaluation timed out while Chromium’s GPU process was using high CPU.
- Node-based warning tracing fails with `ReferenceError: document is not defined` because world creation uses browser canvas APIs.

## Next Move
1. Inspect `/tmp/opencode/mobile-gameplay-active-check.png` for gameplay framing and HUD/control overlap.
2. Recover or restart Chromium and capture an active match with warning stacks and HUD element bounds.
3. Identify and fix the source of `THREE.Color: Unknown color #`, `THREE.Color: Unknown color 3/4/6`; nation and inspected stadium palette definitions are valid.
4. Rebuild and recapture/verify the active match.

## Relevant Files
- `src/world.js`: Stadium/world setup and color construction; likely place to trace invalid color inputs.
- `src/quidditch.js`: Match camera, flight, shooting, aim assistance, and gameplay state.
- `src/ui.js`: Quidditch HUD and gameplay controls.
- `src/styles.css`: Mobile HUD and control styling.
- `src/data.js`: Nation color definitions.
- `src/main.js`: Renderer setup, input, and game flow.
- `/tmp/opencode/mobile-gameplay-active-check.png`: Active-match mobile screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `dist/` has modified generated assets, deleted old bundles, and new bundles.
- Dev server is at `http://127.0.0.1:3002/`; headless Chromium uses remote debugging on port 9222.
- A prior browser snapshot showed 0 errors and 30 warnings, including GPU `ReadPixels` stalls and repeated invalid Three.js color warnings. Latest reload showed only a software WebGL fallback warning and no HUD.

## Objective
- Finish and visually verify the mobile-first broom racing and Quidditch game, focusing on active-match presentation, flight, shooting, and mobile HUD usability.

## Requirements
- Prioritize mobile visuals and approachable flight and shooting controls.
- Check HUD/control overlap, readability, and gameplay framing.

## Decisions
- Retain adaptive renderer resolution and mobile-tuned settings.
- Use eased analog controls and forgiving Chaser hoop aim assistance.
- Keep the Quidditch stadium perimeter wall low to preserve the low-flight camera’s view.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added adaptive pixel-ratio scaling, a larger repositionable joystick, eased controls, Chaser aim assistance, target highlighting, and HUD guidance.
- Captured an active Quidditch match at 390×844: `/tmp/opencode/mobile-gameplay-active-check.png`.
- Confirmed nation colors and the inspected stadium/crowd palettes contain valid hex values.
- Recovered the CDP endpoint and created `/tmp/opencode/cdp-inspect.mjs` to inspect match HUD bounds and log invalid-color console warnings; it has not yet been run.

### Active
- Assess active-match framing, readability, and HUD/control overlap in the captured screenshot.
- Use CDP inspection to capture HUD element bounds and trace repeated Three.js invalid-color warnings to their actual inputs/call sites.

### Blocked
- Prior CDP evaluation timed out while Chromium’s GPU process was using high CPU.
- Node-based warning tracing fails with `ReferenceError: document is not defined` because world creation uses browser canvas APIs.
- The active capture exists, but no current bounds or warning-stack trace has been collected.

## Next Move
1. Inspect `/tmp/opencode/mobile-gameplay-active-check.png` for gameplay framing and HUD/control overlap.
2. Run `/tmp/opencode/cdp-inspect.mjs`; recover or restart Chromium if needed, enter an active match, and gather warning stacks and HUD bounds.
3. Identify and fix the source of `THREE.Color: Unknown color #`, `THREE.Color: Unknown color 3/4/6`; nation colors and inspected stadium palette definitions are valid.
4. Rebuild and recapture/verify the active match.

## Relevant Files
- `src/world.js`: Stadium/world setup and color construction; likely place to trace invalid color inputs.
- `src/quidditch.js`: Match camera, flight, shooting, aim assistance, and gameplay state.
- `src/ui.js`: Quidditch HUD and gameplay controls.
- `src/styles.css`: Mobile HUD and control styling.
- `src/main.js`: Renderer setup, input, and game flow.
- `src/data.js`: Nation color definitions.
- `/tmp/opencode/cdp-inspect.mjs`: CDP script for HUD bounds and invalid-color console logging.
- `/tmp/opencode/mobile-gameplay-active-check.png`: Active-match mobile screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `dist/` has modified generated assets, deleted old bundles, and new bundles.
- Dev server is at `http://127.0.0.1:3002/`; headless Chromium uses remote debugging on port 9222.
- A prior browser snapshot showed 0 errors and 30 warnings, including GPU `ReadPixels` stalls and repeated invalid Three.js color warnings. Latest reload showed only a software WebGL fallback warning and no HUD.

## Objective
- Finish and visually verify the mobile-first broom racing and Quidditch game, focusing on active-match presentation, flight, shooting, and mobile HUD usability.

## Requirements
- Prioritize mobile visuals and approachable flight and shooting controls.
- Check HUD/control overlap, readability, and gameplay framing.

## Decisions
- Retain adaptive renderer resolution and mobile-tuned settings.
- Use eased analog controls and forgiving Chaser hoop aim assistance.
- Keep the Quidditch stadium perimeter wall low to preserve the low-flight camera’s view.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added adaptive pixel-ratio scaling, a larger repositionable joystick, eased controls, Chaser aim assistance, target highlighting, and HUD guidance.

- Created `/tmp/opencode/cdp-inspect.mjs` and confirmed the CDP endpoint responds.

- Assess active-match framing, readability, and HUD/control overlap using `/tmp/opencode/mobile-gameplay-active-check.png`.
- Trace repeated Three.js invalid-color warnings to their actual inputs and call sites.

### Blocked

- The source of `THREE.Color: Unknown color #`, `THREE.Color: Unknown color 3/4/6` remains unknown.

## Next Move
1. Inspect `/tmp/opencode/mobile-gameplay-active-check.png` for gameplay framing and HUD/control overlap.
2. Enter an active match in Chromium at `http://127.0.0.1:3002/` and rerun `/tmp/opencode/cdp-inspect.mjs` to capture HUD bounds and invalid-color warnings.

## Objective
- Finish and visually verify the mobile-first broom racing and Quidditch game, focusing on active-match presentation, flight, shooting, and mobile HUD usability.

## Requirements
- Prioritize mobile visuals and approachable flight and shooting controls.
- Check HUD/control overlap, readability, and gameplay framing.

## Decisions
- Retain adaptive renderer resolution and mobile-tuned settings.
- Use eased analog controls and forgiving Chaser aim assistance.
- Keep the Quidditch stadium perimeter wall low to preserve the low-flight camera’s view.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added adaptive pixel-ratio scaling, a larger repositionable joystick, eased controls, Chaser aim assistance, target highlighting, and HUD guidance.
- Entered an active Quidditch match through CDP and saved a live screenshot.

### Active
- Assess active-match visuals and HUD/control overlap from the screenshot and collected diagnostics.
- Identify and fix recurring invalid Three.js color warnings.

### Blocked
- Warning traces currently point only into bundled Three.js code, so the originating application color inputs have not been identified.

## Next Move
1. Inspect `/tmp/opencode/mobile-gameplay-active-live.png` and the CDP output to assess framing and HUD bounds.
2. Trace the invalid color values reported as `#`, `3`, `4`, and `6` to their originating app inputs; fix them.
3. Rebuild and recapture the active match to verify visuals and confirm the warnings are gone.

## Relevant Files
- `src/world.js`: Stadium/world setup and color construction.
- `src/quidditch.js`: Match camera, flight, shooting, and aim assistance.
- `src/ui.js`: Quidditch HUD and gameplay controls.
- `src/styles.css`: Mobile HUD and control styling.
- `src/main.js`: Renderer setup, input, and game flow.
- `src/data.js`: Nation color definitions.
- `/tmp/opencode/cdp-enter-match.mjs`: Starts a match and collects diagnostics and screenshot.
- `/tmp/opencode/mobile-gameplay-active-live.png`: Latest active-match screenshot.
- `/tmp/opencode/cdp-inspect.mjs`: CDP page inspection script.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `dist/` contains modified generated assets, deleted old bundles, and new bundles.
- CDP viewport is `500×701`, DPR `1`; page URL is `http://127.0.0.1:3002/`.
- `node /tmp/opencode/cdp-enter-match.mjs` enters an active Quidditch match as Chaser.
- Three.js emits repeated warnings including `THREE.Color: Unknown color #`, `THREE.Color: Unknown color 3`, `THREE.Color: Unknown color 4`, and `THREE.Color: Unknown color 6`; captured stacks only show bundled Three.js frames.
- Nation colors and inspected stadium/crowd palettes were previously confirmed as valid hex values.

## Objective
- Finish and visually verify the mobile-first broom racing and Quidditch game, focusing on active-match presentation, flight, shooting, and mobile HUD usability.

## Requirements
- Prioritize mobile visuals and approachable flight and shooting controls.
- Check HUD/control overlap, readability, and gameplay framing.

## Decisions
- Retain adaptive renderer resolution and mobile-tuned settings.
- Use eased analog controls and forgiving Chaser aim assistance.
- Keep the Quidditch stadium perimeter wall low to preserve the low-flight camera’s view.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added adaptive pixel-ratio scaling, a larger repositionable joystick, eased controls, Chaser aim assistance, target highlighting, and HUD guidance.
- Entered an active Quidditch match through CDP and saved a live screenshot.
- Traced invalid Three.js color warnings to `createBroomModel` calls made by `QuidditchMatch.buildTeam` at `src/quidditch.js:172`, rather than the bundled Three.js code.

### Active
- Assess active-match visuals and HUD/control overlap.
- Fix invalid colors passed to broom model materials, then rebuild and retest.

### Blocked
- Exact malformed color arguments in `createBroomModel` are not yet identified; traces point to `src/world.js:729-730`.

## Next Move
1. Inspect `createBroomModel` parameters and material construction at `src/world.js:729-735`; compare with arguments at `src/quidditch.js:172-175` and fix the mismatched values.
2. Inspect `/tmp/opencode/mobile-gameplay-active-live.png` and capture usable CDP diagnostics to assess framing and HUD bounds.
3. Rebuild and recapture the active match; verify warnings are gone and visuals remain correct.

## Relevant Files
- `src/world.js`: Broom model material construction and Quidditch stadium/world.
- `src/quidditch.js`: Match setup, team creation, camera, flight, and shooting.
- `src/ui.js`: Quidditch HUD and gameplay controls.
- `src/styles.css`: Mobile HUD and control styling.
- `src/main.js`: Renderer setup, input, and game flow.
- `src/data.js`: Nation, broom, and role definitions.
- `/tmp/opencode/cdp-enter-match.mjs`: Starts a match and collects diagnostics and screenshot.
- `/tmp/opencode/cdp-trace-colors.mjs`: Temporary CDP script that traces Three.js color warnings.
- `/tmp/opencode/mobile-gameplay-active-live.png`: Latest active-match screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `dist/` contains modified generated assets, deleted old bundles, and new bundles.
- CDP viewport is `500×701`, DPR `1`; page URL is `http://127.0.0.1:3002/`.
- `node /tmp/opencode/cdp-enter-match.mjs` enters an active Quidditch match as Chaser.
- Warnings include `THREE.Color: Unknown color #`, `3`, `4`, and `6`; the new stack traces consistently lead to `createBroomModel` calls in `QuidditchMatch.buildTeam` at `src/quidditch.js:172`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Finish and visually verify the mobile-first broom racing and Quidditch game, focusing on active-match presentation, flight, shooting, and mobile HUD usability.

## Requirements
- Prioritize mobile visuals and approachable flight and shooting controls.
- Check HUD/control overlap, readability, and gameplay framing.

## Decisions
- Retain adaptive renderer resolution and mobile-tuned settings.
- Use eased analog controls and forgiving Chaser aim assistance.
- Keep the Quidditch stadium perimeter wall low to preserve the low-flight camera’s view.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added adaptive pixel-ratio scaling, a larger repositionable joystick, eased controls, Chaser aim assistance, target highlighting, and HUD guidance.
- Identified malformed wood color arguments in `QuidditchMatch.buildTeam` and changed them to arrays of color pairs in `src/quidditch.js`.

### Active
- Build and retest the active match to confirm color warnings are gone and visuals remain correct.
- Assess active-match framing and HUD/control overlap.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run `npm run build`.
2. Re-enter a match with `node /tmp/opencode/cdp-enter-match.mjs`; check warnings and inspect `/tmp/opencode/mobile-gameplay-active-live.png`.
3. Review the captured HUD bounds and gameplay framing; adjust if needed.

## Relevant Files
- `src/quidditch.js`: Team creation and the corrected broom wood color arguments.
- `src/world.js`: Broom model material construction and Quidditch stadium/world.
- `src/ui.js`: Quidditch HUD and gameplay controls.
- `src/styles.css`: Mobile HUD and control styling.
- `src/main.js`: Renderer setup, input, and game flow.
- `src/data.js`: Nation, broom, and role definitions.
- `/tmp/opencode/cdp-enter-match.mjs`: Starts a match and collects diagnostics and screenshot.
- `/tmp/opencode/mobile-gameplay-active-live.png`: Latest active-match screenshot.
- `/tmp/opencode/cdp-trace-colors.mjs`: Temporary CDP script used to trace Three.js color warnings.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `dist/` contains modified generated assets, deleted old bundles, and new bundles.
- CDP viewport is `500×701`, DPR `1`; page URL is `http://127.0.0.1:3002/`.
- `node /tmp/opencode/cdp-enter-match.mjs` enters an active Quidditch match as Chaser.
- The warnings `THREE.Color: Unknown color #`, `3`, `4`, and `6` came from passing a three-string wood array where `createBroomModel` expects two colors; the argument now supplies three color pairs.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Finish and visually verify the mobile-first broom racing and Quidditch game, focusing on active-match presentation, flight, shooting, and mobile HUD usability.

## Requirements
- Prioritize mobile visuals and approachable flight and shooting controls.
- Check HUD/control overlap, readability, and gameplay framing.

## Decisions
- Retain adaptive renderer resolution and mobile-tuned settings.
- Use eased analog controls and forgiving Chaser aim assistance.
- Keep the Quidditch stadium perimeter wall low to preserve the low-flight camera’s view.
- Position match commentary to the left of the minimap rather than centered beneath it.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added adaptive pixel-ratio scaling, a larger repositionable joystick, eased controls, Chaser aim assistance, target highlighting, and HUD guidance.
- Corrected `QuidditchMatch.buildTeam` broom wood colors to pass color pairs expected by `createBroomModel`.
- `npm run build` succeeds; no Three.js unknown-color warnings appeared during active-match entry.
- Captured a gameplay screenshot after forcing the match into play; inspected HUD geometry at `500×701` and found commentary/minimap no longer overlap after the latest CSS change.

### Active
- Rebuild and re-enter a match to verify the latest commentary positioning and review the updated active-play screenshot for HUD overlap and gameplay framing.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run `npm run build`.
2. Run `node /tmp/opencode/cdp-later.mjs` and inspect `/tmp/opencode/mobile-gameplay-active-later.png` and captured HUD bounds.
3. Review the gameplay framing and any remaining mobile HUD/control overlap; adjust if needed.

## Relevant Files
- `src/quidditch.js`: Team creation and broom wood color correction.
- `src/world.js`: Broom model material construction and Quidditch stadium/world.
- `src/ui.js`: Quidditch HUD and gameplay controls.
- `src/styles.css`: Mobile HUD layout; latest commentary placement change.
- `src/main.js`: Renderer setup, input, and game flow.
- `src/data.js`: Nation, broom, and role definitions.
- `/tmp/opencode/cdp-later.mjs`: CDP script that forces active play and captures state/screenshot.
- `/tmp/opencode/mobile-gameplay-active-later.png`: Latest active-play screenshot, taken before the newest CSS change.
- `/tmp/opencode/cdp-enter-match.mjs`: Starts a match and collects diagnostics and screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `dist/` contains modified generated assets, deleted old bundles, and new bundles.
- Previous build succeeded with a Vite warning that the 695.50 kB JavaScript chunk exceeds 500 kB.
- The basic entry script’s 4.5-second wait left the match in `intro`; the later script sets `game.active.introCountdown = -1` to capture `phase: "play"`.
- Previous active-play diagnostics reported `errors: []` and no unknown-color warnings.
